where: The Tide-blessing festival on Pearlmoor Quay (the cutscene after the Tide Gleam is relit)
mood: The going-out song — lantern boats on moonlit water; the quay waltz turned into a cool, glowing, sure ceremony.
core_styles: warm accordion-like pulse-wave lead singing a processional waltz melody
flowing harp arpeggios like lantern light on water over a lush string pad
deep tolling harbour bell on phrase starts
rocking waltz bass like a moored hull
moonlit lantern-boat festival, cool and glowing, celebratory but tender, a hymn-like communal song

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {the harbour bell tolls once, harp ripples outward like the boats pushing off, and the lead lifts the opening phrase of the waltz over a held chord that leads into the theme}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the going-out song: a warm singable waltz melody, steady and sure, harp flowing beneath, the bell marking each phrase like a lantern set on the water}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the same melody again with a high flute descant and fuller strings, as if the whole quay joins in}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a tender turn to D minor, the tide going out, the melody quiet and reflective over harp alone, then the strings swell back toward the major}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the going-out song returns full and glowing with the bell and descant together; the last bar flows straight back into the theme, no ending}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
